Solution 3 is the only correct one; its answer of 200 is confirmed by an independent computation.

**Setup.** Put the external homothety center H at the origin, with the line of centers along the x-axis. The tangents are the lines at angles ±θ to the x-axis. Write c = cos θ and s = sin θ.

**Finding θ and P.** The line of centers is the perpendicular bisector of PQ, so P = (x, y) with |y| = 5. The distances from P to the two tangents are |x s − y c| and |x s + y c|, which equal 3 and 12.
- Their difference gives 2yc = 9, so c = 0.9 and s = √19/10.
- Their sum gives 2xs = 15, so x = 75/√19 and x² = 5625/19.

**The two circles.** A circle with center (a, 0) is tangent to both lines, so its radius is a·s. Requiring P to lie on it gives (x − a)² + 25 = a²s². This rearranges to a²c² − 2xa + (x² + 25) = 0. The two centers a and b are its two roots.
- Sum: a + b = 2x/c² ≈ 42.48.
- Product: ab = (x² + 25)/c², where x² + 25 = 6100/19.
- Then (b − a)² = (a + b)² − 4ab ≈ 1804.9 − 1585.4 ≈ 219.5, so b − a ≈ 14.815.

**The quadrilateral.** The tangency points of the circle centered at (a, 0) lie at x = a c² with y = ±a s c. Those of the other circle lie at x = b c² with y = ±b s c. So U₁U₂V₂V₁ is a trapezoid with parallel sides 2a·sc and 2b·sc and width (b − a)c².

Area = s c³ (a + b)(b − a) ≈ 0.43589 × 0.729 × 42.48 × 14.815 ≈ 200.

**Checking the solutions.**
- Solution 1 assumes the tangents are parallel, which is inconsistent with the circles intersecting. It even finds PQ = 9 instead of 10 and dismisses the mismatch. Its answer of 180 is wrong.
- Solution 2 gives 16√19 ≈ 69.7, which does not match 200. Its algebra is unreliable, so it is wrong.
- Solution 3 gives 200, which matches.

VERDICT 1: REJECT
VERDICT 2: REJECT
VERDICT 3: ACCEPT
